part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in `Streams.AppendableWriter.writeDouble` (gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/internal/Streams.java:94), which is called by `JsonWriter#value(double)`. It rejected non-finite doubles unconditionally, unlike `JsonWriter#value(Number)` which allows `NaN`/`Infinity`/`-Infinity` in lenient mode.

The one-line change makes the check lenient-aware:

```java
if (!writer.isLenient() && (Double.isNaN(value) || Double.isInfinite(value))) {
```

When lenient, the value is rendered via `JsonPrimitive.getAsString()` → `Double.toString()`, producing exactly `NaN`, `-Infinity`, `Infinity` — matching `value(Number)`'s output.

Verified: `JsonWriterTest` (39/39, including `testNonFiniteDoublesWhenLenient` and `testNonFiniteDoubles`), plus `JsonTreeWriterTest`, `MixedStreamTest`, `PrimitiveTest`, `JsonReaderTest`, `JsonElementReaderTest`, `JsonPrimitiveTest` all pass.
